findings.text: gap: §9's done-when requires the fragment to record, for 15 JT-60SA signal sources, the code and wiki chunks chosen before and after the rerank, each labelled relevant or not, with precision at the kept count for each order and the decision spend per source. The landed fragment records only the unit-test-level done-when behaviours in a pass/fail table — no 15-source set, no before/after chunks, no relevance labels, no precision figure, no per-source spend. Neither the fragment nor the run directory (grep for 'precision'/'15' returns nothing outside stream.jsonl) carries this measurement, and the manifest reports no blocker or follow-on for it. The code change itself is correct and gated; the empirical evidence half of the done-when is absent. Coordinator decision: either re-dispatch a node to produce the 15-source before/after precision and spend record, or record the requirement as dropped/waved with a reason.

justifications.durability: the change is guarded and the guard is shown to fire: the bypass mutation (§9's declared control) fails the Jev-order assertion, and the fallback path is exercised by test_code_fetch_falls_back_to_embedding_order_when_unordered, which drives rerank_pool returning an 'unavailable' note and asserts the embedding order survives. The widening is asserted at both fetches (test_code_context_searches_the_wider_pool asserts LIMIT 30; the wiki test asserts the index k is the pool). The spend path is exercised end to end by test_code_fetch_adds_the_rerank_spend_to_the_run_cost_total, which drives WorkerStats.cost and the spend-list drain.
justifications.evidence: the unit-test half is solid and reproduced independently here: the new file's 5 tests pass (§2..§4 of the review work), the full gate `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/discovery` re-ran at head ee146951d and reported 1318 passed, 0 failed, EXIT=0 (gate-head.log, matching the reviewed run's after-suite.log), and the declared negative control reproduces — bypassing rerank_context_chunks so the fetch keeps embedding order reddens test_code_fetch_reranks_with_the_query_and_keeps_jev_order (mine: neg-control.log, 3 failed / 2 passed, EXIT=1). What is missing is the plan's own empirical measure: no before/after chunk selection, no precision at the kept count, and no per-source decision spend for 15 JT-60SA sources exist anywhere in the fragment or the run directory.
justifications.fit: names are capability-based and mechanism-describing (CONTEXT_CANDIDATE_POOL, DECISION_COST_PER_JUDGEMENT_USD, rerank_context_chunks, charge_context_spend, _context_rerank_state, _run_coro); the module comment states why the rerank exists (embedding similarity is a weak relevance signal) without citing any plan or ticket; the test file is named for what it tests; no landed symbol or comment carries a stage label, plan id or attribution. The 'Phase 1/2/3' comments flagged in the file are pre-existing and outside this change's hunks.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the mechanism is implemented exactly as §9 names: both fetches widen to a 30-candidate pool (CONTEXT_CANDIDATE_POOL; _build_code_context_query k=30, wiki query k=CONTEXT_CANDIDATE_POOL) and pass the enrichment query plus each candidate's text to judgment.rerank_pool, keeping the reranked top k (3 for code, the caller's k for wiki). The §9 evidence deliverable is missing. §9's done-when requires the fragment to record, for 15 JT-60SA signal sources, the code and wiki chunks chosen before and after the rerank, each labelled relevant or not, with precision at the kept count for each order and the decision spend per source. The landed fragment (docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-imas-maps/enrichment-context-rerank.html) carries none of that: no 15-source set, no before/after chunks, no relevance labels, no precision figure, no per-source spend. So the code half of the done-when is faithful and the evidence half is absent.
justifications.reuse: the rerank reuses the single shared owner judgment.rerank_pool rather than adding a second rerank, exactly as §9 requires; the wiki scanner imports the shared helper and constants from the signals package at call time (deferred import) rather than duplicating the pool/rerank logic; the fallback logic lives once in rerank_context_chunks and is shared by both fetches.
justifications.scope_discipline: the two-commit diff touches exactly four files — imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py, imas_codex/discovery/signals/scanners/wiki.py, tests/discovery/test_enrichment_context_rerank.py and the evidence fragment — every one inside the node's declared write paths. The declared docs/figures path was correctly left empty (§9's done-when names no figure), and no peer node's path was reached for. No out-of-scope edit to judgment.py, which is why the discarded-cost exposure is carried as a follow-on rather than fixed here.
